To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the damage to the hippocampus, induced by 5-min-long OGD, is determined mainly by the activation of NMDA and AMPA receptors and by the increase in intracellular Ca2+, whereas that induced by 7.5 min of OGD is mainly due to the activation of the latter receptors and the inhibition of tyrosine-phosphoprotein phosphatase.

the anoxic damage of hippocampal neurons, induced by 5- or by 7.5min long exposure to oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), is manifested in the irreversible decrease of the amplitude of field excitatory postsynaptic potentials.
the neuroprotective effects induced by antidepressants and sodium orthovanadates are determined by their influence on expression of neurotrophic factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neuroprotective action of antidepressants with respect the anoxic damage of neurons in the CA1 area of the hippocampus.
the mechanisms of neuroprotective effects induced by antidepressants and their combination with sodium orthovanadat.
the possibility of the use of antidepressants as neuroprotective agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the neuroprotective action of antidepressants with respect the early damage to hippocamp neurons is determined, at least to a considerable degree, by their ability to intensify the expression of neurotrophic factors, which, in turn, decrease the functional activity of the NMDA receptor and the consequences of the OGD induced increase in the intraneuronal Ca2+ concentration.
the chronic introduction of antidepressants into the experimental animals resulted in a decrease in the OGD-induced damage to the hippocampal neurons.

the neuroprotective action of antidepressants is determined by the activation of neuroprotective mechanisms in the brain, which are based on the intensification of expression and activity of neurotrophin proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antidepressants, in the case of preliminary introduction, are capable of weakening the OGD-induced damage of hippocampal neurons.

chronic antidepressants, which are widely used in the clinical practice, are able to prevent the development of irreversible damage to neurons of the hippocampal formation in case of acute anoxic influences.

the anoxic damage of hippocampal neurons, as well as its modification resulting from chronic influences of antidepressants, is associated with a complex of processes in neurons, which is determined by the activity of NMDAreceptors, AMPA-receptors, calcium channels, and tyrosine phosphatase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chronic administration of antidepressants is a promising method of neuroprotection of the hippocampus against the damage induced by OGD.
antidepressants are able to modify the consequences of early anoxic damage to the hippocampus.
chronic introduction of antidepressants can result in neuroprotection of neurons in the hippocampus, which can be used in the development of new methods of treatment for ischemic brain injuries.
